Who produces lithium in Chile and who owns them?
Thought for 1s

The table has 4 rows: 2 for “Lithium carbonate”, 1 for “Lithium chloride” and 1 for “Lithium hydroxide”. Albemarle Corp. is named as an owner in 2 of the 4 rows; its stated share is 100% in each. Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A. is named as an owner in 2 of the 4 rows; its stated share is 100% in each.

Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A. is named as an owner in 2 of the 4 rows; its stated share is 100% in each.

These rows list the facilities, capacities, and the exact ownership stakes as printed in the USGS Minerals Yearbook 2019 (primary statistical source). No buyer information is included in the source.

Missing link: the downstream buyers of the Chilean lithium chemicals are not captured in our current records. A supply-chain disclosure from the producers or trade-flow data would fill that gap.

Lithium facilities in Chile — USGS Minerals Yearbook 2019
Operator	Owners and shares, as printed	Commodity, as printed	Location	Capacity, as printed
Rockwood Litio Ltda.	Albemarle Corp., 100%	Lithium carbonate	La Negra I and II plants, Antofagasta Region	44,000 metric tons
SQM Salar S.A.	Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A. (SQM), 100%	Lithium carbonate	Salar del Carmen plant, Antofagasta Region	70,000 metric tons
Rockwood Litio Ltda.	Albemarle Corp., 100%	Lithium chloride	La Negra I and II plants, Antofagasta Region	6,000 metric tons
SQM Salar S.A.	Sociedad Química y Minera de Chile S.A. (SQM), 100%	Lithium hydroxide	Salar del Carmen plant, Antofagasta Region	13500 metric tons

Every cell is copied from the USGS table as printed. Capacity is capacity, not production. The table names no buyers. USGS Minerals Yearbook, volume III (Area Reports: International), country chapters, Table 2. Structure of the mineral industry (Table 2) ↗
